races.name: Burke's Clonbur 3-Y-O Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Divine Believer
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's hold-up operator has flat form on soft ground but steps up sharply in trip to hurdles; form figure of 5 on good ground on debut is workable, and the stable's T14 strike rate of 4/24 gives some confidence, though a big field of 16 debutants and exposed rivals makes this a speculative assignment for Mike O'Connor.

runners_data.name: Another Day Done
runners_data.note: Won a bumper at the Curragh and arrives with Anthony McCann in decent form (1/4 T14); a genuine back-of-the-field type by nature, the congestion of hold-up horses in this field means James Smith on the 5lb claim will be forced to race closer to the pace than ideal, which is not where this horse does its best work.

runners_data.name: Chairmanforlife
runners_data.note: John Harrington's yard is operating at 2/32 over the past fortnight and this horse has a mid-pack bumper profile — fourth on Good To Soft on the most relevant run — but the absence of a jockey listed is notable and the step to 2m2f hurdles is uncharted territory for a horse whose best bumper effort was at 2m1f.

runners_data.name: Misty Cove
runners_data.note: The most interesting prominent type in the race, wearing a tongue-tie and ridden by Eoghan Finegan (5lb claim); won a bumper on soft and placed again on that surface, so the Good To Yielding should not inconvenience, and Gavin Cromwell's runners at this meeting deserve respect even with the stable's 0/35 T14 stat.

runners_data.name: Point Star
runners_data.note: Has only run once (fourth in a 2m2f bumper on good ground at Tipperary), so the switch to hurdles is speculative, but that single piece of form is directly relevant to today's trip and surface; Thomas O'Connor's 7lb claim makes this a modestly interesting each-way angle without much evidence to back it up.

runners_data.name: Armillary
runners_data.note: A complete unknown — no form on record, no listed last run date, and a small yard (0/0 T14) in Harry Sexton's 7lb-claim hands; the lightly-raced warning is warranted and this horse must be rated on trust alone without any going, style, or distance evidence.

runners_data.name: Camp Verde
runners_data.note: Placed nowhere in three hurdle starts including a pulled-up — form of 0U8 is concerning; a true late-runner by inclination, the numerical excess of hold-up types forces Josh Younge (7lb claim) into a closer-to-pace role than suits, making a positive outcome dependent on circumstances that this horse's record does not support.

runners_data.name: Step By Step
runners_data.note: No publicly available form, no last-run date, and only a tongue-tie in headgear to note — Aidan Kelly takes the ride for a stable (T14: 1/2) with a thin recent record; must be treated as a full unknown and cannot be assessed on pace, going, or trip grounds.

runners_data.name: Wills History
runners_data.note: Another debutant with no published form or last-run information; Calum Hogan's 5lb claim for Brian McMahon (0/5 T14) offers little trainer support, and without any evidence of style or going preference, this runner is unquantifiable beyond the surface observation.

runners_data.name: We're Out Of Aces
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott sends this unraced type (0/0 OR) here with Ethan O'Sullivan (7lb claim); the stable is in solid form (5/34 T14) and Elliott's debutants at this level deserve a note, but without any form to anchor an assessment, this remains a significant unknown in a wide-open field.

runners_data.name: Bell Ex Too
runners_data.note: Five bumper runs have produced no wins and a best finish of fifth; a natural hold-up runner whose form on soft (9th) and good (6th, 7th) is unremarkable — the redistribution into midfield simply compounds the structural disadvantage, and Paddy Cody's 7lb claim for a small stable (2/6 T14) adds little confidence.

runners_data.name: Montevetro
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner and therefore the most tactically pivotal horse in the field; Philip Donovan has a good handle on what he has, and Denis Hogan's 0/25 T14 stat is the only soft spot — Montevetro should lead throughout and how long he sustains it over 2m2f on Good To Yielding will define the entire race shape.

runners_data.name: Neon Eyes
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell runner wearing a hood, last ran just six days ago and went clear to second at a previous start on good ground; the hold-up style means this horse needs the pace to collapse late, but a recent run and prior placed form give it a sliver of each-way credibility from the back if the fractions quicken.

runners_data.name: Sonny Corleone
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's hold-up bumper type has been placed twice from five runs but has not won; the stable's form (5/34 T14) is the strongest angle here, though no jockey is listed and a step up to hurdles from a flat-form profile of 9-7-4-4-10 is uninspiring without a clear positional upgrade.

runners_data.name: Matada
runners_data.note: A Gavin Cromwell hold-up runner who hasn't raced in 111 days — the layoff is the headline concern, and three bumper runs produced a best of 12th on good; the return from a long absence in a 16-runner maiden hurdle on Good To Yielding with no jockey listed is too much uncertainty to overcome.

runners_data.name: Captain Con
runners_data.note: Six runs in bumpers without winning and a best of sixth; headgear (blinkers) are listed, which may sharpen focus, and Alan O'Sullivan's 5lb claim for Noel Meade (1/31 T14) is a modest angle — but consistent back-end finishes on good ground and a history of not threatening make this a hard-to-back hold-up type in this shape.

races.paceDynamic: Montevetro is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 16-horse maiden and should face no serious challenge for the lead, giving Philip Donovan complete control over tempo from the first hurdle on Good To Yielding ground at Ballinrobe. With one horse setting a sustainable, uncontested gallop over 2m2f, the pace is unlikely to be either scalding or falsely slow — it will be honest but manageable, meaning the leaders will not be softened up sufficiently for a dramatic late flourish. This shape historically favours horses that can travel prominently or at least close to the pace, ready to pounce from the second-last, rather than true deep closers who need a fast-run race to make up ground. The field carries more hold-up horses than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — Camp Verde, Another Day Done, and Bell Ex Too are genuine late-runners by nature but will be squeezed into midfield roles in this shape, reducing their effectiveness and making their task harder than their natural style would suggest. Overall, prominent racers and horses with the tactical speed to sit just off Montevetro and strike from two out are best served here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Montevetro Leads, Prominent Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Montevetro sets a steady, uncontested pace and prominent types travel smoothly within striking range throughout.
scenarios.body: Montevetro's control keeps the race honest without burning off those sitting just behind, and when he ties up or is challenged from two out, a horse like Misty Cove or Chairmanforlife with the tactical speed to track the leader has the simplest route to the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Montevetro dictates a genuinely moderate tempo and is never truly tested, conserving enough for the run-in.
scenarios.body: A crawl early on the Good To Yielding ground would play directly into the hands of a confident leader, and with no pressing rival, Montevetro could simply coast home before the closers wind up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Type Weaves Through
scenarios.trigger: If Montevetro sets a workable pace but the prominent contingent get into a competitive battle from two out, opening gaps for a sharp mover from midfield.
scenarios.body: A scrappy finish around the home turn at Ballinrobe can create pockets of space, and a horse like Divine Believer or Neon Eyes arriving late from a tracking position could benefit if the front group tire into each other.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Montevetro or the prominent group set a genuinely strong gallop that softens the leaders sufficiently for deep closers to run through beaten horses.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given the lone front-runner scenario and the fact that Camp Verde, Another Day Done, and Bell Ex Too are displaced from their true role — they would need atypically strong fractions to reach their natural advantage zone.

watchPoints.text: Montevetro — watch whether Philip Donovan elects to coast in front or is chased wide early; if he gets an uncontested lead with a steady tempo, the race is run entirely on his terms and prominent types must close the gap from two out rather than further back.

Camp Verde, Another Day Done, and Bell Ex Too — all three are confirmed hold-up horses squeezed into midfield by the race shape; if any of them get hampered or find no room in a 16-runner field racing closer than natural, they become significant non-runners in terms of their true chance.

Misty Cove — the tongue-tie is appearing in a hurdling context for the first time; if the headgear causes any early keenness or settles her less cleanly than in bumpers, her prominent position could turn from asset to liability on the undulating Ballinrobe track.

We're Out Of Aces and Step By Step — both Gordon Elliott and Aidan Howard debutants are completely unexposed; in a maiden this open, an unlisted or unknown runner from a top stable can land a blow first time, and watchers should note how quickly each settles and jumps at the opening flights.

Matada — 111 days off the track is the longest absence in the field; Gavin Cromwell is capable of producing fit horses first time back, but any sign of greenness or sluggishness jumping will confirm this run is conditioning-focused rather than win-targeted.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Brave Lady
runners_data.note: Peter Fahey's mare has finished second in four of her last five runs — rock-consistent but yet to win; she's a genuine prominent type who is most likely among the redistributed trio to secure an actual forward position given her track record of jumping and travelling well on similar going, though her inability to convert placed efforts is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: The Dotski
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead runner returning from 195 days off, which is the standout fitness query here; showed ability in flat form and drops into hurdles, but a layoff of this length on soft ground over 2m2f for an unexposed mare means she needs everything to fall right.

runners_data.name: Goodgollymissholly
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott handler in T14 form (5/34) and this mare won over 16f on good ground — a naturally forward-going type who is unlikely to get her preferred front-rank position with so many rivals wanting the same berths, which materially softens her chance in this particular race shape.

runners_data.name: Rosarian
runners_data.note: Josh Halley's four-year-old has placed at 19f on good ground and drops slightly in company here; a prominent-style runner with a cleaner pace profile in the field than the redistributed trio, giving her a genuine chance of landing a forward position if the scrimmage resolves quickly.

runners_data.name: Lunar Majesty
runners_data.note: C A Murphy runner with a consistent record of mid-table finishes (three 6ths, a 5th, a 3rd) over 2m-2m4f on similar ground; the lack of a win from seven starts suggests she finds a way to be involved without threatening, and a 7lb claimer aboard adds minor doubt.

runners_data.name: Maximillian Lady
runners_data.note: Pulled up on her last start, but her two prior runs include a second over 16f on soft and a second over 19f on good; the hold-up style suits a genuinely run race and the step back from a P run is the key risk, though 88 days off could mean a freshened-up performer.

runners_data.name: Katie Can't Count
runners_data.note: Mullins runner whose two starts show a fall and a fourth — very limited profile; a natural front-runner whose instincts are likely to be frustrated in this congested field, making it hard to assess what her ceiling is or whether she'll handle being shuffled back.

runners_data.name: Ronnie's Rascal
runners_data.note: Mullins four-year-old with an OR of 104, the highest rated runner here, and a second over 22f on good ground among her placings — she has the class and the stamina profile; a 7lb claimer (Sean Cleary-Farrell) keeps the price honest, but this is a strong entry from the stable if she jumps cleanly.

runners_data.name: Hashtag Doyen
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old mare returning from 28 days off with a modest form string including a P and a 5th; the midfield style is genuine but the class level suggested by her form string makes it hard to see her troubling the principals here unless the race falls apart.

runners_data.name: Lexenna
runners_data.note: Three runs yielding a 6th, 7th, and 6th — no form to suggest she can reverse those placings without significant improvement; Darren Collins yard at 0/2 T14 and no listed jockey adds to the concern around market support.

runners_data.name: Tara Boe
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old mare 16 days off her last run, which resulted in an 8th over 20f on good ground; hood headgear worn and a long journey back to competitiveness at this level given the age and flat recent figures.

runners_data.name: Santa Paula
runners_data.note: Placed twice over 16-18f on good ground for Dermot McLoughlin; a consistent placed performer but stuck in a pattern similar to Brave Lady — finding the frame without winning — and her best form is short of this trip.

runners_data.name: Certosa
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile with a second over 16f on good ground in recent form; 7lb claimer Tom Kelly aboard and the 20d freshen-up is modest, but she's been competitive on similar surfaces and the trip here is a step up she may appreciate.

runners_data.name: Mia In Milan
runners_data.note: 94 days since last run, and form figures of 5th, 13th, and 10th do not inspire confidence; hold-up style is genuine but she would need to find significant improvement to feature.

runners_data.name: Kilbarry Alexy
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner — 251 days off and returning from a 9th and a 3rd, so fitness and jumping fluency over hurdles are genuine queries; if she bounces back to form and jumps well, she controls the shape of the entire race, but a lengthy absence at this level is a live concern.

runners_data.name: Sea Limit
runners_data.note: Two runs producing a 9th and a 9th on good ground — no evidence of the ability required; midfield runner who has not shown any sign of threatening and has no listed jockey confirmed, which compounds the doubt.

runners_data.name: Mastertown Miss
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard top selection: David Harry Kelly's four-year-old showed a second over 16f on soft and a fourth on good — hold-up profile suits a truly run race over this trip; 18 days since last run keeps fitness fine, and Peter Smithers (5lb) has been in decent form, making this the most compelling profile if the pace is honest.

runners_data.name: Carleys Lilly
runners_data.note: John Patrick Ryan's five-year-old has five hurdle starts including a third over 18f on good and a fourth over 16f — consistent hold-up performer; OR of 92 is workable in this field and recent frequency of runs (23d) suggests she is fit and race-ready, making her a reasonable each-way type if the race is truly run.

races.paceDynamic: Kilbarry Alexy is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner maiden hurdle over 2m2f on Good to Yielding ground at Ballinrobe, and with no genuine rival to press her early, she is likely to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front. Behind her, a significant cluster of naturally prominent types — Brave Lady, Goodgollymissholly, and Katie Can't Count — have been redistributed to midfield on the pace map because the field simply cannot accommodate that many horses in the front rank; in practice, Brave Lady's solid recent form and Peter Fahey's record make her the likeliest of the three to actually secure a forward berth, while Goodgollymissholly and Katie Can't Count may find themselves shuffled back against their instincts. This field contains more genuine pace than a lone leader scenario can mask: several prominent types will be jostling for position in the first half-mile on softening ground, creating an honest if not breakneck tempo that will test stamina rather than reward pure finishing speed. On balance, the race shape favours hold-up horses with proven stamina at this trip and going, provided they can get a clean passage through a busy midfield.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Kilbarry Alexy dictates an uncontested tempo and the prominent scrimmage behind her burns out rivals.
scenarios.body: Kilbarry Alexy sets a measured pace with no genuine rival willing to go with her, and the horses fighting for prominent positions behind expend energy that tells in the home straight on this soft-ish ground; a confirmed hold-up type who has settled quietly gets the clearest run to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle Rewards Fresh Legs
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution scrum among Brave Lady, Goodgollymissholly, and Rosarian creates a contested pace that burns the leaders off.
scenarios.body: Multiple naturally prominent mares fighting for the same berths elevate the tempo beyond what Kilbarry Alexy would set alone, and horses who have settled just off the pace with fresh legs — particularly those with strong recent runs — pounce from the home turn.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Sweep From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough throughout that only confirmed hold-up horses with stamina survive.
scenarios.body: A heated first half creates a strung-out field on the run to the final hurdle, and deeper closers who have been patient in the last quarter of the field benefit most as the front rank ties up on the testing surface.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse — Dawdle Then Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If Kilbarry Alexy sets a crawl and the prominent group all tuck in, producing a sprint finish off a slow pace.
scenarios.body: A lack of genuine tempo makes this a tactical race decided in the final two flights, heavily favouring the sharpest jumper and most agile mover at the finish; hold-up horses who need the race truly run are disadvantaged.

watchPoints.text: Kilbarry Alexy's jumping is the fulcrum of this race — if she fidgets or makes a mistake at an early hurdle after 251 days off, the pace dynamic collapses entirely and the race becomes a sprint, which changes the winner profile dramatically.

Monitor market moves for Ronnie's Rascal: as the highest OR horse in the field (104) trained by Mullins at 3/17 T14, any significant support at the off would signal stable confidence in a mare who has placed at 22f and has obvious class grounds for winning.

Brave Lady's redistribution means she may attempt to push forward from a wide draw or poor position early — watch for signs of trouble in running in the first half-mile as she attempts to secure her natural prominent berth against several rivals with similar intentions.

Goodgollymissholly and Katie Can't Count are both naturally forward-going types likely to be caught in traffic; if either burns energy fighting for position through the opening mile, their chance in the straight is compromised regardless of ability — a clean early position is essential.

The going at Ballinrobe is officially Good to Yielding for this race but later cards on the card are Yielding — ground is clearly deteriorating through the afternoon, which may increasingly favour horses with proven stamina and prior form on softer surfaces as the ground gives further.

runners_data.name: Take The Free
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in good heart after a course win last time in form 8-621, handles this going well (4 from 4 on similar), with trainer Bolger posting a 1/4 strike rate in 14 days — 67 days off is not a worry given the recent winning run.|
runners_data.comment: Ran to winning effect most recently and has going experience to call on, but a lengthy 67-day absence is a notable query and he carries 156 lb against a competitive field; that layoff makes him harder to place with confidence.

runners_data.name: Crossing The Bar
runners_data.note: Returns after a huge 523-day absence, which is the defining concern — lightly raced at nine and completely unknown quantity returning from such a lengthy layoff; the going rating is flagged unknown and the form string ends with a slash indicating the break began mid-sequence.|
runners_data.comment: Crossing The Bar showed a fine turn of foot when winning three starts back, and has experience of today's trip and conditions to back up a rating of 118, making him a genuine danger; the sole concern is whether a 523-day absence leaves him short of peak fitness.

runners_data.name: Mickey Cohen
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good recent form (1-2-4 from last three hurdle starts) who handles good-ground conditions well, trained by Noel Meade whose 14-day record is modest here; the 61-day gap is manageable and the 2m6f trip looks within range of his form at 2m4f.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 11 of 14 on our figures and with his trainer in wretched form at 1/32 over the past fortnight, Mickey Cohen is hard to fancy despite a win three starts back; fourth last time out after 61 days off makes the return uncertain too.

runners_data.name: Luck Between Us
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer on a sharp upward curve after consecutive placed efforts capped by a win (form 607-12), with the step to 2m6f on Good To Yielding looking ideal given his last win came over this trip on good ground; apprentice Niall Moore (5lb) is a booking to note.|
runners_data.comment: Ran well last time out with a second, and a winner two starts back, but that seventh three starts back tempers expectations; has run over today's trip and going, and 157 lb is a stern test for a gelding ranked mid-field here.

runners_data.name: Jupiter Du Gite
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up horse rated 116 whose two most recent runs both produced second-place finishes over similar trips, and whose form on good ground reads 0W2P from five runs — talented but carries the burden of an apprentice claimer and has yet to win on this surface combination.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent in recent starts, Jupiter Du Gite has finished second in each of his last two outings and has run over today's trip and going, giving him every chance to go one better here; he carries 162 lb but our rating of 129, top of these, makes him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Better Times
runners_data.note: Has a single hurdle win to his name on soft ground but his recent form reads 14U-47 with two poor efforts latest; a true hold-up type whose natural rear-of-field position is occupied by several rivals, meaning he is unlikely to replicate the conditions that suit him most, and the 104-day break adds uncertainty.|
runners_data.comment: Better Times has experience of today's distance and going, and a win features in his recent starts, but he was last seen finishing seventh and has been off the track for 104 days; 155 lb is no help either.

runners_data.name: Mr Dibbs
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who holds an uncontested lead card, winning over 2m6f on good ground (form includes a win at that trip); ridden by a 7lb claimer Alix Balfe and trained by the busy Gavin Cromwell, last ran just 13 days ago — if he controls his own fractions, his stamina gives him every chance.|
runners_data.comment: Mr Dibbs won three starts back but has since finished eighth and sixth, and with his trainer yet to strike from 38 attempts in the past fortnight and ranked 12 of 14 on our figures, he faces a stiff task despite going experience and a return after just 13 days.

runners_data.name: Strange Currency
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse whose record shows 0 wins and 0 places from eight recent runs, and whose best finish on good ground is a fifth — his redistribution into midfield reflects that real closers are crowding the rear, and his raw form figures give little confidence at OR 104 regardless of race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with finishes no better than fifth in recent outings, Strange Currency faces a stiff ask on these figures — ranked 13 of 14 — though he has run over today's going before and returns after a 32-day break carrying 150 lb.

runners_data.name: Arcland
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up performer in the form of his life after a win at 2m and a second last time out, handling good ground strongly (2W3P from eight recent good-ground starts); Gavin Cromwell's second string but arguably the in-form horse in this race, and the Strand Scorecard's top selection at medium confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Arcland won two starts back and was second three starts back, showing a consistent profile over today's going, and his 15-day turnaround looks spot on; the main concern is a trainer who has drawn a blank in 38 attempts over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Ehteyat
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner at OR 121 but his recent form string (3230-P) culminating in a pull-up is a serious red flag, and his historical form over this trip and going combination (0W2P from 13 runs on good) suggests he rarely translates ability into wins; ridden by a 7lb claimer.|
runners_data.comment: Placed twice in his last five starts — third three starts back and second four starts back — Ehteyat rates a serious threat here off a 22-day break, our rating of 123 putting him second of 14; the main concern is that pulled-up latest effort.

runners_data.name: Free Flow
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up type whose recent hurdle form reads 090-64 — modest figures that place him at the bottom of the handicap on OR 97, and only seven days since last run raises freshness questions; a genuine hold-up horse who will struggle to express that style fully with several rivals jostling for rear-tracking positions.|
runners_data.comment: Free Flow has run over today's going and returns on a quick seven-day turnaround, but he has been winless in his last five starts, his recent efforts including a fourth and a sixth, and our rating of 110 suggests he holds more ability than his official mark of 97 implies.

runners_data.name: In The Minus
runners_data.note: Progressive young four-year-old (form 5-5013) who won over 2m1f on good ground and placed over 2m4f most recently; hold-up in style but carries decent form for the grade at OR 116, and the 23-day turnaround for trainer Cawley is workmanlike — the big field suits if he can find a clean route.|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out after winning two starts back, In The Minus arrives on the back of reasonable form and has run over today's going before, though a hefty 159 lb burden and a ranking of sixth from fourteen in the field are the checks on his chance.

runners_data.name: Pilgrims Walk
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up type off a 32-day break whose last two runs produced a second and a third over 2m4f and 2m6f on good ground respectively (form 080-23); rated just OR 97 but carries a 3lb apprentice claim for Shane O'Callaghan and is the most likely of the redistributed hold-up horses to actually track up into a midfield position given his recent forward-running tendencies.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last of the 14 on our figures, Pilgrims Walk faces a stiff task under 140 lb, with his trainer in poor form at 1/26 over the past fortnight; experience over today's trip and going offers some small crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Needs Must
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old returning from 178 days off for Gordon Elliott, whose stable is firing at 5/34 in 14 days; won over 2m4f on soft ground but his three most recent runs (two hurdles form runs) show a fall and a non-completion — the long absence and unfinished business over hurdles mean this is speculative.|
runners_data.comment: Needs Must landed a win three starts back but has since fallen and finished unplaced, leaving his form hard to read; 178 days off the track adds further uncertainty, though he carries a competitive weight and his rating of 118 keeps him respected here.

races.paceDynamic: Mr Dibbs is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, he is set to control fractions from the front at Ballinrobe over 2m6f on Good To Yielding ground — a surface that rewards stamina and jump accuracy rather than pure finishing speed. The pace he sets is likely to be sustainable rather than scorching, as he has no rival pressing him into an unsustainable gallop, and a controlled tempo over this trip on softening ground historically compresses the field into a convoy shape through the middle stages before the test becomes one of staying power from three out. Four runners — Better Times, Strange Currency, Pilgrims Walk, and Free Flow — are genuine hold-up types redistributed into midfield positions on the map because the field holds more true closers than can all settle to the rear in a 14-runner hurdle at this pace; of these, Pilgrims Walk is the most likely to actually secure a forward tracking position given his recent prominence, while Better Times and Strange Currency are confirmed off-the-pace operators who will not naturally hunt up. The tactical verdict is clear: a patient hold-up or stalking-midfield horse who can travel smoothly behind a steady Mr Dibbs and produce a clean round of jumping in the final mile will be best served, favouring horses like Arcland and Jupiter Du Gite who possess the class and going form to challenge at the business end.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Stayers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Dibbs sets an unchallenged, measured gallop that keeps the field together until the final circuit, releasing pressure for hold-up and midfield closers.
scenarios.body: Mr Dibbs controls at a tempo that suits horses travelling within themselves, and from three out the race becomes a stamina test where Arcland's solid good-ground form and proven 2m+ finishing effort gives him the edge over a tiring field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Dibbs dictates an honest but unforced gallop and the field fails to close the gap in the straight, leaving him in front longer than expected.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing or able to press Mr Dibbs early, he gets a dream lead and the 2m6f trip on Good To Yielding tests closers whose jockeys leave too much to do; at OR 101 he is lightly weighted and has a win over this trip on similar ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racers Score
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just slow enough to bunch the field, bringing prominent-style horses Take The Free and Mickey Cohen into contention on the bridle turning for home.
scenarios.body: Both Take The Free and Mickey Cohen carry solid similar-going form and are ridden by capable jockeys who can place them ideally just off the leader before delivering their challenge between the final two hurdles; at OR 113 and 100 respectively they are tractable enough to follow Mr Dibbs without burning too much fuel.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Shakes It Up
scenarios.trigger: If an uneven early pace or mid-race incident causes the field to fragment, giving a hold-up horse who threads through the carnage a route to an unexpected win.
scenarios.body: Strange Currency or Better Times, if allowed to settle to the rear as their true style demands, could benefit from a messy race that produces a strong final-furlong finish from off the pace; however their redistributed midfield map positions and recent below-par form figures temper expectation significantly.

watchPoints.text: Watch Mr Dibbs in the early stages — if Alix Balfe (7lb claimer) allows him to stride on entirely unchallenged, the controlled pace he sets could prove very difficult for hold-up horses to bridge in the straight, especially if the Good To Yielding ground firms slightly through the card.

Arcland is 10 years old and his most recent win came over 2m rather than this 2m6f trip — if the pace is genuinely searching in the final mile, watch whether his stamina holds at the top of the weights carrying 162lbs.

Crossing The Bar returns from 523 days off and is an unquantifiable risk in a competitive 14-runner handicap — if he shows signs of rustiness at the early hurdles, he could bring down or impede horses tracking him from behind.

Ehteyat's recent pull-up despite carrying the highest OR in the race (121) is a market watch — if he trades short in-running before weakening, it signals the pace or ground conditions are tougher than the official going description suggests and may be a useful real-time read for the closers.|

Needs Must (Gordon Elliott, 178 days off) is one to monitor in the betting market — if Elliott has had time to school this five-year-old properly over hurdles following his earlier fall, a market move late on would be meaningful given the strength of the yard's recent 14-day record.|

runners_data.name: Cobra Queen
runners_data.note: Front-runner with strong similar-going record (6/6 on Good-going variants), De Bromhead sending her here fresh at 33 days; rated highest of the pace-makers at OR 118 and sets the race up on her own terms, though style-fit tag (0.92) is flagged as a form-shape concern should she be asked to race differently.
runners_data.comment: Cobra Queen arrives here in solid heart after back-to-back thirds, and with experience of today's trip and going she appeals as the one to beat off 166 lb, though she remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Camlin Park
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer for John McConnell, 16 days since last run and tongue-tie fitted; zero wins from five outings on similar going limits confidence, but her proximity style means she will be involved early and could pinch a place if Cobra Queen weakens.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Camlin Park nonetheless catches the eye on going and distance experience, and our rating of 116 suggests she is better than her official mark of 109; the chief concern is a recent string of disappointing efforts, including two pull-ups.

runners_data.name: Theflyingbee
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who has placed four times from six runs on comparable ground and has been knocking on the door with back-to-back runner-up finishes; races prominently and the 2m6f Ballinrobe trip suits her thorough stayer's profile under a conditional.
runners_data.comment: Theflyingbee has been remarkably consistent, finishing second twice and third twice in her last four starts, and our rating of 124 marks her out as a serious threat here; the main concern is that she remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Walkingmayotomilan
runners_data.note: Won over 2m2f on Good ground at this track which is a key positive; Shane Markey (7) takes the ride and the midfield style means she needs things to develop in front of her, but she is unexposed at this trip and her mark of OR 101 looks workable.
runners_data.comment: Walkingmayotomilan won last time out but that single success punctuates a largely disappointing recent record of unplaced runs and a pull-up, and our rating has her a clear last of eleven in this field; she has run over today's distance and going, and the 32-day break at least means she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Sound Judgement
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott representative who won over course-and-distance equivalent going (2m4f Good) and has placed heavily on similar surfaces; races prominently and the consistent placed record (3W3P from seven similar-going runs) makes her a natural fit for the dominant shape here.
runners_data.comment: Sound Judgement won two starts back and was third three starts back, showing she can mix it at this level, but a sixth last time out after 38 days off raises a fitness query; the 153 lb burden is a stiff ask as she drops back into midfield contention.

runners_data.name: Nothing Hectic
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who won over 2m2f Good last time but has since weakened; Ricky Doyle takes a tricky ride from the back of the field and she will need a stronger pace than Cobra Queen is likely to set to get into contention at 2m6f.
runners_data.comment: Nothing Hectic won last time out and also took a win five starts back, but the two seventh-place finishes and a pulled up in between temper expectations; she has run over today's trip and going, and 152 lb is a stern test of whether she can sustain that recent upturn.

runners_data.name: St Anthonys Corner
runners_data.note: 345 days off the track is an enormous concern and the fade-in-finish flag compounds that worry; OR 83 is the lowest in the field and only one career run in similar going, making her a very difficult proposition to support at any price.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and absent for nearly a year, St Anthonys Corner faces a stiff ask here, ranked 10 of 11 on our figures despite carrying 140 lb; experience over today's trip and going offers slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Run For The Border
runners_data.note: True hold-up type who has placed four times from nine similar-going starts and finished second over 2m6f Good recently — the form is there, but being nudged forward into midfield by the race structure means she cannot deliver her natural late run, and the STYLE_FIT flag (0.91) reflects that compromise.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Run For The Border makes it hard to build a case; that said, she returns quickly on 11 days' rest, has run over today's trip and going before, and her third two starts back shows she can hit the frame.

runners_data.name: You Make Me Smile
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard top selection at low confidence; a genuine hold-up operator by nature whose best form comes from the rear, but with surplus hold-up types in this field she cannot settle where she wants, and the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) must temper enthusiasm despite consistent placed form on similar ground.
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in her last four starts — third last time out, and a winner five starts back — You Make Me Smile arrives on familiar going after a 36-day break, though 146 lb is a stern burden and an eighth-of-eleven ranking suggests she faces stiffer opposition here.

runners_data.name: Bossy Bird
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare for Gibney, placed twice from four similar-going outings but never won; Harry Sexton (7) rides and she needs pace to chase at 2m6f — the controlled tempo under Cobra Queen makes her finishing kick less likely to land a decisive blow.
runners_data.comment: Bossy Bird shaped with promise when second three starts back, but she has drifted out of the frame in both outings since and remains winless in her last five starts; the 150 lb burden is a further ask, even if she has experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: She'll Be Kept
runners_data.note: Won twice from four similar-going runs including back-to-back wins at OR 112 and has strong form at 2m2f-2m4f; amateur Mr E M Nugent (7) is the query, but if she gets a clear run from hold-up she is capable of picking off tired rivals and the improving form profile is eye-catching.
runners_data.comment: She'll Be Kept arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has run over today's trip and going, so conditions hold no fears; the main question is whether 160 lb blunts her momentum after 38 days off.

races.paceDynamic: Cobra Queen is the one confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner mares' handicap hurdle over 2m6f on Good to Yielding ground, and with no genuine challenger for the lead she can dictate at a sustainable, unhurried gallop — the kind of tempo that rewards front-of-house racing throughout. Camlin Park, Theflyingbee, and Sound Judgement will press for prominent positions just off Cobra Queen, creating a competitive but controlled early order rather than a searching test. You Make Me Smile and Run For The Border are natural hold-up types who will find their true positions at the rear compromised by the volume of prominent runners filling the midfield, meaning they are unlikely to secure the ground they ideally want and their redistribution to midfield is map necessity rather than tactical preference. With a single pace-maker controlling the tempo, this shape strongly favours horses racing prominently who can track the leader, conserve energy on the long Ballinrobe circuit, and produce a clean jump at the last — the prominent-to-prominent profile is the most advantageous, with genuine late closers at a structural disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cobra Queen Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Cobra Queen gets a clean early lead and dictates an even, unchallenged gallop on the Good to Yielding surface.
scenarios.body: Cobra Queen settles into her rhythm in front with Camlin Park and Theflyingbee tracking just off her, and the pace never truly quickens enough to expose her stamina at 2m6f; with no horse able to collar her before the last, her front-running record on similar ground becomes decisive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Cobra Queen's gallop is just quick enough to stretch the field but she runs out of fuel approaching the final hurdle.
scenarios.body: A horse like Theflyingbee or Sound Judgement, sitting a length or two off the pace and travelling within themselves, pounces as the leader momentarily flattens out, with their consistent recent form on similar ground giving them the edge in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to soften up the leaders and open a gap for a horse coming from slightly further back.
scenarios.body: Walkingmayotomilan or She'll Be Kept, both capable of finishing with purpose on Good to Yielding going, travel in midfield and benefit from a clear run up the rail to overtake a tiring Cobra Queen; the 2m6f trip suits both on form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops at a truly strong gallop and the leaders are fully cooked turning for home.
scenarios.body: You Make Me Smile or Run For The Border, both genuine hold-up types pushed into midfield by the race shape rather than preference, would need an unusually strong pace to close the gap — a scenario that is structurally unlikely given a single front-runner and several style-displaced horses filling the middle ground.

watchPoints.text: Watch Cobra Queen's jumping at the first two hurdles — if she gets a clean passage and settles immediately, the race is effectively hers to control; any early errors could let Camlin Park or Theflyingbee steal the march.

You Make Me Smile is the scorecard top at low confidence and is a natural hold-up type structurally displaced to midfield — monitor whether Sean Cleary-Farrell (7) tries to drop her out regardless or accepts the midfield slot, as that tactical decision materially affects her chance.

She'll Be Kept's two recent wins give her the strongest finishing form in the field but Mr E M Nugent (7) is an amateur pilot over 2m6f — watch how she travels turning for home; if still on the bridle two out she becomes a live each-way threat.

Run For The Border ran just 11 days ago and is a true hold-up horse mapped forward by the race shape — short-turnaround hold-up horses in this position often fail to find their rhythm, making her a horse to monitor early for signs of comfort or restlessness.

St Anthonys Corner has not run for 345 days and carries the fades-in-finish flag — if she appears conspicuously well before racing she is a speculative interest, but in the absence of that signal she is best used as a pace informant rather than a betting proposition.

runners_data.name: Affinity Rock
runners_data.note: Consistent front-runner with a clean similar-going record (3 runs, 0 wins but 3 places), handled Good and similar surfaces well; Carl Millar's 5lb claim is a useful weight assist and Cian Collins sends her here on a competitive 22-day turnaround — she is the natural pace anchor at OR 122.
runners_data.comment: Affinity Rock arrives in fine fettle after a sequence of three consecutive placings, including second two starts back and third last time out, and has experience of today's trip and conditions; the concern is that 161 lb is a sizeable burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Carried With Love
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced five-year-old returning from a 222-day absence for Jonathan Sweeney, last seen finishing well off the pace on Heavy; she is a natural front-end operator whose best form has come from prominent positions, though the prominent congestion in this field means she is unlikely to secure that berth as freely as she would want.
runners_data.comment: Consistent place-getter who has finished third on three occasions in recent starts, with a second one start back showcasing her best, though she returns after 222 days off and carries a hefty 161 lb; has experience over today's trip and going, and her rating of 127 makes her the one to side with.

runners_data.name: Straight Home
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins' representative carries the stable's 3-from-17 14-day form and has just one similar-going run to reference; the tongue tie is noted and Sean Cleary-Farrell's claim takes weight off — capable of better than that single hurdles run suggests if she settles in the prominent pack.
runners_data.comment: Straight Home won two of her last four starts and brings solid recent form into this, having run over today's trip and going; the chief concern is whether 161 lb proves too stiff an impost against a strong field.

runners_data.name: Cooke's Lass
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott runner returning from 364 days off, a significant freshness flag in a beginners' chase; the hood is fitted and her one similar-going start showed promise with a second, but jumping inexperience after a year off makes this a speculative hold-up assignment.
runners_data.comment: Cooke's Lass returns after a 364-day absence carrying 161 lb, and her recent form — pulled up last time, a fall three starts back, and a second before that — gives a mixed picture; going experience helps, but she's winless in her last four starts and fitness on comeback day is the key query.

runners_data.name: Giorgia Rose
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with five similar-going runs all producing placed or in-frame finishes, though zero wins from those efforts is telling; Emmet Mullins' 0-from-5 14-day record is mild concern, and the tongue tie and hood combination suggests she needs some restraint — reliable at keeping tabs on proceedings but may lack a finishing gear.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Giorgia Rose makes little appeal at the weights carrying 161 lb, though she has run over today's trip and going before and those three consecutive third-place finishes one, two and three starts back hint at a degree of consistency.

runners_data.name: Joya Del Mar
runners_data.note: Strong recent form with two wins from nine similar-going starts and three places — Joya Del Mar's natural prominent style suits this race shape well, and the 33-day break looks routine; Alix Balfe's 7lb claim eases the burden and this mare's course-type experience (nine similar-going runs) is the most substantial in the field.
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back and a winner three starts back, Joya Del Mar has run over today's trip and going and returns after 33 days, but a fifth last time out and a ranking of sixth in this field of nine on our rating suggest she faces a stiff task under 161 lb.

runners_data.name: Ad Caelum
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator at OR 104 who won over 24f on Good ground but has posted two pulled-up finishes in recent outings, raising serious fitness or confidence questions; Alan O'Sullivan's 5lb claim helps but a horse arriving here with back-to-back non-completions must be treated with caution over this demanding trip.
runners_data.comment: Twice pulled up in her last two starts is the obvious concern, but Ad Caelum showed her quality with a win earlier in this recent sequence, and she arrives on a fair turnaround of 21 days, with experience of today's distance and going and a our rating of 114 lending substance to her claims.

runners_data.name: Cherry Red
runners_data.note: Won last time out on Good over 18f and has a win to her name on similar going; a natural prominent racer whose style is compromised by the prominent congestion in this field, making it harder for her to replicate front-end form — the 61-day break is moderate and D M Christie's small yard numbers provide limited strike-rate confidence.
runners_data.comment: Cherry Red arrives having been unplaced last time out after a win the start before, and with a pulled up and an unseated also in recent starts, consistency is a real concern; rated lowest of the nine runners, she faces a stiff task off 161 lb, though she does have experience of today's going.

runners_data.name: Survivors Sister
runners_data.note: At OR 102 with a win from 21f on Heavy and placed twice from seven similar-going runs, Survivors Sister carries the Strand Scorecard danger tag with justification; Philip Donovan takes the ride after a 108-day break, and the natural prominent style from a handy position suits this race shape — the staying trip and yielding ground align with her best form profile.
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Survivors Sister has posted just one win in her last five starts alongside a pulled up and two mid-field finishes, and 108 days off the track adds a fitness query; that third one start back offers a sliver of encouragement, and she has going experience to call on.

races.paceDynamic: Affinity Rock is the confirmed, sole front-runner here and with no genuine challenger likely to push hard for the lead from the outset, she can dictate a controlled, measured gallop across this 2m7f trip on Yielding ground — a surface that rewards jumping fluency over raw speed. Behind her, a clutch of prominent types — Giorgia Rose, Joya Del Mar, Straight Home, and Survivors Sister — will jostle for the best positions in the chasing pack, and that congestion becomes genuinely dangerous between the second-last and last fence where competitive room will be compromised. The field carries more prominent-racing types than the race shape can accommodate; Cherry Red and Carried With Love are both natural prominent operators who are likely to find that territory already occupied, forcing them further back than suits their best form. This race shape — a single pacesetter controlling an honest but not scorching tempo on energy-sapping ground over a staying trip — fundamentally favours a prominent racer who settles close to the leader without burning fuel early, possesses clean jumping, and can produce a sustained rather than explosive finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Affinity Rock Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Affinity Rock jumps cleanly, dictates an honest tempo unchallenged, and the chasing pack burns energy fighting for position.
scenarios.body: Affinity Rock settles into her rhythm from the front, and the Yielding ground gradually stretches the field, with prominent types who contested position tiring late; a well-placed prominent racer who settled smoothly behind her without incident emerges to challenge or prevail. This shape rewards Survivors Sister and Joya Del Mar, who have the tactical speed to track from a handy position and sustain their effort up the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pace Scramble Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion behind Affinity Rock causes interference or jumping errors between the 3rd and 2nd last, unsettling the chasing order.
scenarios.body: With four runners competing for the same tracking positions, any mid-race incident reshuffles the field and opens the door for a horse who has been switched wider and produced a cleaner round of jumping; this suits a horse with a sound recent form profile who avoids the traffic. Carried With Love, returning from 222 days off but a natural front-end type operating on suitable going, could capitalise if the scramble clears a path, though the long layoff is a genuine caveat alongside the redistribution pressure.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lone Pacesetter Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Affinity Rock's controlled front-running becomes an unassailable lead in the final mile as the ground saps her rivals' energy.
scenarios.body: On genuinely Yielding ground over this long trip, a front-runner who has jumped well and conserved energy can find late rivals flat-footed when they move to close — the ground does the damage for her. Affinity Rock's three-run course-similar-going record shows consistent placing and she handles these conditions, making a front-to-finish scenario viable if the chasing pack misjudges their move.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scramble produces a truly strong pace that burns out the front group, allowing a hold-up runner to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires the mid-race congestion to generate genuine pace pressure that Affinity Rock cannot fully control — a lower-probability outcome given she is uncontested at the head of affairs. Ad Caelum and Cooke's Lass are the hold-up profiled runners, but Ad Caelum has shown a marked drop in form lately with pulled-up finishes, and Cooke's Lass has not run for 364 days, making this the least reliable shape.

watchPoints.text: Affinity Rock's jumping — if she fiddles an early fence under Carl Millar and loses momentum, the tightly-grouped prominent pack behind her will immediately seize the initiative and reshape the entire race.

Prominent congestion between the 3rd and 2nd last fence — with Giorgia Rose, Joya Del Mar, Straight Home, and Survivors Sister all seeking the same tracking position, a bump or checking move here could eliminate multiple contenders simultaneously.

Cooke's Lass jumping on debut over fences after 364 days off — a novice chaser returning from a full year away on Yielding ground at 2m7f is a meaningful safety and race-flow risk for horses travelling immediately behind her.

Carried With Love's ability to find a prominent pitch — 222 days off and a natural front-end runner in a race where that space is already taken; if she is shuffled back further than her form demands, her chance effectively dissolves regardless of fitness.

Going drift to Yielding specifically for the 5:40 race (earlier races run on Good To Yielding) — the ground is softer than the card headline suggests, which amplifies the stamina premium and may expose runners whose form is built on better surfaces.

runners_data.name: Three Tribes
runners_data.note: A 9-year-old hold-up horse with reasonable similar-going figures (2/2 sim-going) but the redistribution note reflects a genuinely rear-running style competing in a field where the back of the race is severely congested; Barry T Murphy's runner has been off 56 days and moderate recent form (0P1-PP) makes a winning return unlikely.
runners_data.comment: Three Tribes has pulled up in three of his last five starts and ranks 17th of 19 on our figures, making him very hard to fancy; he does have going experience and showed he can win, but that form feels distant against this company.

runners_data.name: Subset
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and returning from a massive 470-day absence, this 12-year-old's going preference is unknown and the lengthy layoff makes fitness a serious question mark; treat with significant caution until reassessed in running.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and returning from a 470-day absence, Subset faces a stiff ask on comeback — yet he has run over today's trip and going, and that second last time out hints at ability, with our rating of 95 suggesting he holds stronger claims than his official mark implies.

runners_data.name: Il Silenzio
runners_data.note: Top-rated at OR 100 and carrying 168lbs, this hold-up horse has 1W1P from two similar-going runs including a recent Soft-ground win, and the step up in trip to 2m7f should suit his staying profile if Conor Smithers can navigate the traffic.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and has previous form on today's going, but our rating of 91 trails several rivals and 168 lb is a stern burden; the 38-day absence is a mild query for a gelding who has shown he can produce when ready.

runners_data.name: Not So Serious
runners_data.note: A 5-year-old midfield runner whose recent win over 2m2f on Good ground is on the short side for this 2m7f test, but T14 trainer form of 1/3 is modest encouragement; 11 days since last run suggests freshness.
runners_data.comment: Not So Serious boasts strong claims on our rating, ranked third of 19 runners, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; however, his recent form is erratic — a winner three starts back, he has since unseated and finished ninth in his last two starts.

runners_data.name: Ladies Well
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's top selection: an exemplary similar-going record of 8-from-8 (2W4P), recent wins and places on comparable surfaces, and a hold-up style that fits the likely race shape perfectly — Alan O'Sullivan's 5lb claim adds further appeal at 166lbs.
runners_data.comment: Ladies Well arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going, yet our rating of 91 sits seven pounds below her official mark and she carries 166 lb, which may test her stamina.

runners_data.name: Hit The Frame
runners_data.note: A prominent runner for J P Flavin, off 118 days which is the longest absence in the field; his four similar-going runs produced no wins or places, and the lengthy layoff combined with a disappointing recent record makes him a speculative each-way proposition at best.
runners_data.comment: Hit The Frame has failed to win in his last four starts and, ranked 14 of 19 on our figures, is hard to fancy; 118 days off the track adds another question mark, though he has distance and going experience and does own a win in recent form.

runners_data.name: Las Brisas Boy
runners_data.note: A 5-year-old prominent runner with back-to-back placed efforts (2-2) in his most recent runs, both on Good ground; the step up to 2m7f on Yielding is new territory for him and will need to be seen to be believed.
runners_data.comment: Consistent place-getter but winless in his last five starts, Las Brisas Boy has back-to-back runner-up finishes to his name and has experience of today's going, though a hefty 156 lb burden may test his resolve in a competitive nineteen-runner field.

runners_data.name: Mistyburn
runners_data.note: Strand Scorecard danger: a hold-up horse with a solid similar-going record (1W3P from 10-14 qualifying runs) and an OR of 89 that puts him in competitive territory; Mr R Sugrue's amateur claim is worth noting in a big field, and recent form (31-663) includes a win and a third.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out shows Mistyburn retains some ability, and he has run over today's distance and going before, but two consecutive sixths in the interim and a trainer striking at just 4% recently are harder to ignore under a hefty 157 lb burden.

runners_data.name: Tomas O Maille
runners_data.note: A 9-year-old hold-up type with a stamina fade flag and a grim recent string of 9P9P83; 14 days between runs and no wins from 11 similar-going starts paint a discouraging picture for this trip.
runners_data.comment: Tomas O Maille steps back up sharply in our ratings, topping the 19-runner field, and his third last time out — his best recent effort — suggests he retains ability; yet to score in his last six starts, though 14 days is a sharp enough turnaround and the distance and going hold no fears.

runners_data.name: Island McCoo
runners_data.note: No jockey declared which is an immediate concern, but the horse has shown versatility (1W2P from 9-11 similar-going starts) and a win from a hold-up position; the missing rider information must be factored in before any assessment is finalised.
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out and fourth two starts back, Island McCoo's recent form is modest, though a win four starts back shows he can find the winner's enclosure; he has distance and going experience to call on, but 157 lb is a stern test.

runners_data.name: Swing Time
runners_data.note: This horse's true running style is hold-up, placed in midfield on the map only because the rear of the field is overcrowded; a STYLE_FIT of 0.93 tempers expectations significantly, and three years of failing to win from midfield on Good ground (0W0P from 4-5 runs) does not help.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulled up two runs back, Swing Time faces a stiff ask off 146 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a rating of 87 suggests connections may still believe there is more to come.

runners_data.name: Fr Gilligansvoyge
runners_data.note: The most impressive course-going record in the field — 3W7P from 12 similar-going starts, a 13-year-old who clearly thrives at Ballinrobe; Sarah Kavanagh's 7lb claim is a small asset, and his prominent style makes him a natural early threat to Kilashee's lead.
runners_data.comment: Ranked a long way below the assessments of his rivals on our figures, Fr Gilligansvoyge is hard to fancy at the weights carrying 158 lb, yet his recent form reads well with three wins in his last six starts and a second last time out.

runners_data.name: Kilashee
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner whose uncontested lead is the pivotal tactical fact of this race; flagged as a fader in the closing stages, off 56 days, with a recent form string of 067-PP and poor similar-going figures (1W2P from 8-9 runs), Kevin Healy's 7lb claim does not adequately offset the age (11) and stamina concerns.
runners_data.comment: Kilashee has struggled badly in her last two starts, pulling up on both occasions, and remains winless in recent starts, so there are obvious concerns; yet she has run over today's distance and going before, and our rating of 93 suggests she retains more ability than her official mark of 80 implies.

runners_data.name: Set The Tone
runners_data.note: A 5-year-old with a legitimate similar-going record (1W3P from 8-9 runs) and a recent win at this trip, but his true style is hold-up and his mapping to midfield understates how far back he is likely to race; STYLE_FIT of 0.93 means his chance in the dominant race shape is discounted.
runners_data.comment: Set The Tone shaped well enough when runner-up last time out, but a sixth two starts back and a pulled-up effort in recent starts make her hard to fancy at the foot of the rankings, and 145 lb is a stiff ask despite her familiarity with today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Zolpharine
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old hold-up horse trained by John Patrick Ryan (T14: 2/14) with two recent wins on Good ground, though the last run produced a zero (0) and the horse was well beaten on a similar surface last time; similar-going record is moderate (2W3P from 11-15) and warrants monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Zolpharine has back-to-back wins three and four starts back, but two disappointing efforts since, including an unplaced run last time out, and our figures rank him well adrift of this field carrying 156 lb.

runners_data.name: Walkmethroughit
runners_data.note: A midfield runner with no wins and no places from 5-7 similar-going starts, and a recent form string of 77PP-7 that offers nothing to work with; no jockey declared adds to the concerns around this 6-year-old.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last of 19 on our figures, Walkmethroughit's recent form — two pull-ups sandwiched between a string of sevenths — makes him extremely difficult to fancy, though he has run over today's going before and returns after a 49-day break.

runners_data.name: Reve Inoui
runners_data.note: A prominent runner returning from 97 days off for J P Flavin's yard (T14: 0/2); no wins or places from four similar-going runs and a recent sequence of PP54-8 provides little reason for optimism despite the prominent style suiting the likely race shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 97 days off, Reve Inoui nevertheless catches the eye on our rating of 98, and he has experience over today's trip and conditions — the concern is whether that lengthy absence blunts his edge against a deep field.

runners_data.name: The Little Yank
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old who is genuinely a hold-up horse, though the congested rear means he will race in midfield against his natural instinct; STYLE_FIT of 0.92 means his chances in the dominant hold-up-suits scenario are genuinely compromised, and recent form (P-3370) combined with age limits expectations.
runners_data.comment: The Little Yank shaped with promise when third in consecutive starts, and his rating of 100 gives him a strong claim as a leading threat carrying 154 lb; the concern is he arrives just four days after his last run, winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: U Asking Me
runners_data.note: A 9-year-old with both a stamina fade flag and a redistribution tag — this hold-up horse will be racing out of role in midfield on Yielding ground over 2m7f; 0W0P from five similar-going starts and a recent form of -7P08F make a productive run very hard to envisage.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 13 of 19 here, U Asking Me does at least bring distance and going experience to the table and returns on a reasonable 28-day break, though a fall last time and a pulled-up finish among his recent outings give obvious cause for caution.

races.paceDynamic: Kilashee is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of 19, and with no other genuine pace horse to pressure him, he is likely to bowl along at a sustainable, self-regulated gallop over the Yielding 2m7f trip — a surface and distance combination that will test stamina thoroughly in the closing stages. The redistributed types — The Little Yank, U Asking Me, Swing Time, and Set The Tone — are true hold-up horses pushed into midfield on the map simply because the rear is overcrowded; none of them are natural pace-pressers, so Kilashee's lead is unlikely to be contested. Fr Gilligansvoyge, Las Brisas Boy, Hit The Frame, and Reve Inoui will likely fill the prominent positions behind the leader, creating a well-strung-out contest where the real race begins in the final mile. A solo, unhurried gallop on Yielding ground over a stamina trip strongly favours genuine hold-up horses with proven form in this going, allowing them to slide through and pick off a fading leader — the profile of a patient, ground-handling chaser with a strong finishing effort is the one to be on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kilashee Sets, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Kilashee's uncontested lead produces a steadily run race that collapses in the final two fences as the Yielding ground bites.
scenarios.body: Kilashee dictates at a comfortable tempo through the early stages, but his flagged finishing fade catches up with him from three out as the Yielding ground exacts its toll; hold-up horses with proven similar-going form surge past the tiring leader to fight out the finish. This shape ideally suits Ladies Well, whose 8-from-8 similar-going record and recent winning form mark her as the standout beneficiary of a patient-to-prominent race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Fr Gilligansvoyge and Las Brisas Boy push up to join Kilashee early and the pace becomes genuinely strong, burning off the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Fr Gilligansvoyge's outstanding course-form record (3W7P from 12 similar-going runs) and Las Brisas Boy's prominent style mean they could move up behind Kilashee and create a faster, more pressured gallop than the lone-leader scenario implies. A stronger pace on Yielding ground would paradoxically suit a horse with exceptional stamina who can be placed closer to the pace, and Fr Gilligansvoyge's record on this going type is difficult to dismiss.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Muddle, Traffic, Melee
scenarios.trigger: If the 19-runner field causes significant traffic issues through the middle stages, with hold-up horses blocked as Kilashee fades and no one gets a clear run.
scenarios.body: With so many genuine hold-up types compressing into a midfield cluster behind Kilashee, interference and traffic problems are a live risk on Ballinrobe's tight track; horses drawn wide or with adaptable jockeys who can find a gap early will benefit disproportionately. Island McCoo and Set The Tone, who have each shown the ability to produce placed efforts from midfield when given a clear path, could capitalise if the main dangers are baulked.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Slips Away
scenarios.trigger: If Kilashee bowls along completely unchallenged at an ultra-slow tempo and the field fails to quicken on the Yielding surface, allowing him to steal the race.
scenarios.body: Though Kilashee is flagged as a fader, a truly crawling pace on a tiring surface can occasionally allow a front-runner to steal enough of a lead that chasers cannot close the gap in time. This shape is the least likely given Kilashee's age, poor recent form, and recorded finishing fade, but a bungled pace read from the midfield pack could gift him an unassailable advantage.

watchPoints.text: Watch Ladies Well's early positioning — if Alan O'Sullivan can slot her smoothly into midfield without using her up in the 19-runner scramble, her 8-from-8 similar-going record makes her a serious threat from the second-last fence onward.

Kilashee's jumping at the early fences is critical — if he takes a heavy knock or is forced to steady, the entire pace dynamic collapses and genuine hold-up horses could find themselves in front too soon on Yielding ground.

Fr Gilligansvoyge's rider Sarah Kavanagh may push up aggressively to track Kilashee given his outstanding Ballinrobe record; if he does so, watch whether he can sustain that effort over the final mile in the Yielding conditions.

With five runners tagged [REDISTRIBUTED] and several more natural hold-up horses, the midfield from fence three to fence seven is likely to be unusually congested — any horse losing its position or being baulked in this zone should be noted for future reference.

Il Silenzio's 168lbs is the joint-highest weight in the race and his hold-up style on Yielding ground over 2m7f warrants watching to see whether he can still produce his usual finishing effort under that burden in the closing stages.

runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts but Leave In Secret has been knocking on the door, finishing second last time out and third two starts back, and he arrives here fresh on 34 days' rest, with experience of today's trip and going, carrying 166 lb for a race in which our figures rate him very narrowly off the top.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Arizona

runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 14 of 19 on our figures, Phoenix Arizona is hard to fancy despite carrying 149 lb, though a second and a third in recent starts show he can hit the frame, and he has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Claude
runners_data.note: Second confirmed front-runner wearing tongue-tie and blinkers for Sarah Joanna Connell; 0W1P from seven similar-going starts tells the story — likely to help make the race but vulnerable once the stamina test bites in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Ranked top of the field on ratings and returning on a good 29-day freshener, Claude has experience of today's trip and going and shaped with promise when third three starts back; yet to win in recent starts is the concern.

runners_data.name: Stoneyford Lady
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's stable in strong form (T14:4/24); wears a tongue-tie and pads under Danny Power (4lb) and has placed on soft ground (1W4P similar going) — sits in the prominent group but is a natural one-two off the pace runner who could avoid the worst of the front-end carnage.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Stoneyford Lady at least showed some promise with a third two runs back, though a fourth last time out and a weight of 156 lb make progress hard to find; she has run over today's trip and going, which offers some grounding.

runners_data.name: Roccabaker
runners_data.note: Midfield operator returning from 145 days off; has won and placed on soft and heavy ground (1W2P from 5 similar-going runs) suggesting stamina is genuine — the layoff is the question mark, but David Harry Kelly has him in the field so presumably fit enough.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 18 of 19 on our figures, Roccabaker makes this look a tough ask, and 145 days off the track adds further doubt; she has run over today's distance and going, and a win in her last five starts shows she can find the line first.

runners_data.name: Sayitfirst

runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 11 of 19 here, Sayitfirst carries 154 lb against her, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns after a 32-day break with something to prove.

runners_data.name: Political Stance

runners_data.comment: Political Stance has been in grim form of late — unplaced and pulled up in his two most recent outings — and rated 15th of 19 on our figures, he is hard to fancy under 146 lb; a second three starts back and experience over today's trip and going are slim consolations for a gelding yet to win in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Bossing It
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a 0W1P similar-going record; six-year-old for David M O'Brien who placed over 17f Good last time (2nd) — the stamina test at 2m1f on Yielding may suit, and Josh Williamson takes off useful weight.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Bossing It does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and 26 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh; however, a 150 lb burden and a ranking of 13 of 19 in the field make a big run hard to call.

runners_data.name: Ballybrittas

runners_data.comment: Third last time out after winning two starts back, Ballybrittas has experience of today's trip and conditions, but a 160 lb burden and a trainer firing at just 4% in the last fortnight are real negatives against him here.

runners_data.comment: Won last time out and has previous experience over today's trip and going, but her rating of 106 ranks her fifth of nineteen and a weight of 166 lb is a stiff burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Lady Doyanne
runners_data.note: Scorecard danger from De Bromhead's in-form yard (T14:4/24); wears a tongue-tie and Alan O'Sullivan (2lb) rides — prominent style with a 0W3P similar-going record showing consistent placing form, and step up beyond 16f is the one question over stamina.
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in recent starts, Lady Doyanne has run over today's trip and going before and arrives 34 days fresh, giving her every chance to go one better; the concern is she remains yet to win in her last five starts.

runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 16 of 19 on our figures, Fedneys Park faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's trip before and a return from 89 days off can occasionally spark improvement.
